reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents coverage of PM Modi and President Trump's roadshow to Sabarmati Ashram, with a motorcade, public crowds, event signage and performances. The subscription request is ordinary channel engagement and is not linked to an investment offer, payment requirement, credential request or other deceptive mechanism. The limited sampled frames and unavailable ASR/OCR leave unsampled content unassessed.

citations.quote: PM Modi and President Trump's roadshow to Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, Gujarat
►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.

opening.argument: Judge, the description pairs an action with a benefit: viewers are directed to subscribe through a link and told they can get the latest updates. That is a low-barrier solicitation, even though it is attached to roadshow footage. The evidence does not establish where the shortened link leads or what happens after a viewer follows it, so the visible event alone should not settle how to treat the linked invitation.

citations.quote: ►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.
Get the latest updates :bell: from PM's Office: news, speeches, public outreach, national events, official state visits, PM's foreign visits, and much more...

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's motorcade and performance examples establish what appears in sampled frames, not what the subscription link does. Calling the request ordinary channel engagement assumes the link behaves as described; the supplied description gives its invitation and claimed benefit but does not verify its destination. Nor do the sampled frames resolve that question.

citations.quote: ►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The proposed benefit is updates from a channel, not a free asset, payment or withdrawal. The description explicitly presents the link as a subscription to the official YouTube channel, while the title identifies roadshow coverage. An unverified possibility about the link's destination is not evidence of a deceptive claim or claim flow.

citations.quote: ►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.
Get the latest updates :bell: from PM's Office: news, speeches, public outreach, national events, official state visits, PM's foreign visits, and much more...
PM Modi and President Trump's roadshow to Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, Gujarat

opening.argument: The relevant caution is the combination of official-sounding identity, several outbound destinations and a shortened subscription link. The description invites viewers to get updates, then supplies routes to follow. None of that proves the destinations are deceptive, but the visible roadshow does not validate the links either. A judge should assess the solicitation in the description, not let the public-event imagery stand in for verification of it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that its cited frames depict an event, but they cannot authenticate an outbound link. Its statement that no payment or credential request appears in the supplied material addresses only the visible invitation; it does not establish the destination or subsequent steps. That uncertainty matters most for the shortened subscription URL.

citations.quote: ►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An external link and an official-sounding description are not, together, evidence of deception. The listed destinations are presented as the office's website and social channels; the only stated benefit is updates. No cited source offers a reward, asks for money or credentials, or shows a claim procedure. The frames support the stated event context.

citations.quote: You can also connect with us on the official PMO website & other Social Media channels
Get the latest updates :bell: from PM's Office: news, speeches, public outreach, national events, official state visits, PM's foreign visits, and much more...

opening.argument: Judge, this is not solely passive event coverage. The title draws viewers to a roadshow, and the description turns that attention toward subscribing and connecting through other channels. The public scenes can make that invitation more credible, but they do not answer whether the linked route delivers what the description promises. Treat the call to action as part of the video's function, not as irrelevant text beside it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the footage as the video's main context, but the description also asks viewers to act. Its cited performance and motorcade frames show the roadshow; they do not determine the role of the linked invitation. Describing that invitation as ordinary does not itself verify the destination or negate its promotional purpose.

citations.quote: ►Subscribe https://goo.gl/C3hVED | to Prime Minister Office's official Youtube channel.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a channel does not make its event coverage a scam. The title identifies a specific roadshow, and the sampled scenes show crowds and a motorcade consistent with that subject. The description asks for a subscription to receive updates, not participation in a reward or payment scheme. Its call to action does not establish the deceptive mechanism this argument needs.
